title: Environment IAM patterns and evidence automation guide
body:
Purpose:
This doc consolidates recommended IAM role matrices, minimal policy templates, environment-specific access rules (hosted / dedicated / private), and an evidence-automation checklist for audits and SIEM exports. It is intended as a pragmatic engineering-friendly reference for product, infra, and security teams preparing RBAC v2 rollouts and compliance evidence.

Scope and assumptions:
- RBAC v2 refers to the updated role model in our control plane (roles, role-sets, scope binding).
- Environments: Hosted (Redwood-managed, multi-tenant), Dedicated (customer-reserved GPU pools), Private (VPC/on-prem with customer control plane).
- Principle: least privilege + clear separation of duties + auditable artifacts for every change.

Quick role matrix (digest):
Columns: Role | Typical personas | Allowed API surfaces | Environment differences
1) infra-admin | Infra engineers, platform ops | full control over infra resources, node pools, networking | Hosted: no host-level access; Dedicated: limited host control via support workflow; Private: broad (customer may have additional controls)
2) model-ops | ML engineers, model-owners | model upload, versioning, rollout, quantization profiles | Hosted: model artifacts stored in Redwood bucket; Dedicated/Private: customers can restrict artifact push to org-owned registry
3) app-developer | Product engineers | create routes, request/usage config, per-route SLOs | Hosted: can create public routes per org quotas; Dedicated: route creation scoped to dedicated pools; Private: routes must be approved by infra-admin in air-gapped installs
4) security-auditor | Compliance, internal audit | read-only access to audit logs, evidence bundles, SIEM exports | All envs: read-only; Private requires network path to control-plane audit endpoint
5) support-agent | Support team | customer-facing incident tools, read logs, create tickets | Hosted: limited to org-scoped logs, redacted PII; Dedicated: elevated view with customer consent; Private: access via customer-provided support channel

Full matrix (text table) available as a separate sheet (linked_artifacts). Use the above as canonical mapping for RBAC v2 role-to-surface bindings.

Policy template examples (minimal, copy-paste friendly) - replace placeholders:
1) Role: model-ops-minimal (JSON-style policy expressed for control plane engine)
{
  "version": "2024-01-01",
  "statements": [
    { "action": ["models:upload", "models:list", "models:get"], "resource": ["arn:redwood:model:${org}:${model}"] },
    { "action": ["models:promote"], "resource": ["arn:redwood:model:${org}:${model}:version/*"], "condition": { "role_binding": "canary" } }
  ]
}

2) Policy stub: readonly-audit
{
  "version": "2024-01-01",
  "statements": [ { "action": ["audit:read", "siem:export"], "resource": ["arn:redwood:audit:${org}:*"] } ]
}

SIEM export / audit schema (recommended minimal fields):
- event_id (uuid)
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- actor_id (user principal id)
- actor_email (redacted if PII policy applies)
- actor_role (role snapshot at time-of-event)
- action (canonical action id, e.g., models:upload, routes:create)
- resource_arn
- resource_type
- request_id (trace id)
- request_latency_ms
- outcome (success|failure)
- client_ip (redacted for hosted per PII policy)
- region
- env (hosted|dedicated|private)
- extra (freeform JSON blob with exec context, e.g., model size, seq_len)

Export considerations by environment:
- Hosted: strip client_ip when actor is end-user or when cookies/PII present; default export cadence 1m; retention policy: 90 days hot, 13 months cold.
- Dedicated: export includes node-level metrics (GPU id, instance type) to help SRE triage; retention per contract.
- Private: customer controls export; provide schema and an s3-compatible drop; recommend signing with customer KMS.

Audit evidence automation checklist (for SOC/ISO/Customer reviews):
1) Evidence catalog: ensure every deploy, role-change, and policy update emits an evidence record with links to config diff, author, timestamp, and approval ticket.
2) Sign-off automation: require two approvers for infra-admin role bindings (unless emergency), tracked via Jira and recorded in evidence bundle.
3) Snapshot exports: weekly snapshots of role-binding table and active policies; stored to evidence-bucket/${org}/snapshots/YYYY-MM-DD.json
4) Hashing & provenance: sign snapshots with control-plane key and include signature metadata in evidence bundle.
5) Automated SIEM mapping: evidence exporter should map audit events to the recommended schema and drop to customer SIEM or Redwood-owned SIEM depending on contract.

Runbook: automating role change evidence (summary steps)
- Step A: create role-change PR in infra repo (github link required)
- Step B: CI runs policy lint, runs simulated access tests against a mock org (linear ticket created if tests fail)
- Step C: upon CI pass, create Jira approval request tagged SEC-AUDIT and route to two approvers
- Step D: when approvals are recorded, control-plane API applies binding and emits audit event + evidence bundle (PR diff, approver IDs, timestamp, CI artifacts)
- Step E: evidence automation lambda archives bundle to evidence-bucket and triggers SIEM push microjob (or notifies customer webhook for Private).

Environment-specific gotchas and recommended mitigations:
- Hosted: never grant infra-admin to non-infra teams; use role-sets to grant temporary elevated access via ephemeral tokens; enforce SCIM sync and MFA.
- Dedicated: clearly separate who can spin up/terminate capacity vs who can change model rollouts. Add "capacity-admin" role. Maintain per-customer change advisory.
- Private: expect customers to require offline evidence transfer; support signed bundles and HSM-wrapped keys. Provide an on-prem agent that can push signed audit bundles to the customer’s SIEM endpoint.

Testing and validation suggestions:
- Periodic RBAC fuzz tests: simulate common persona actions and assert outcomes equal expected permissions; fail the snapshot if deviations > threshold.
- SIEM schema conformance checks: nightly job to validate exports against schema and report missing critical fields.
- Evidence reproducibility: pick random evidence bundles and attempt to reconstruct the state (policy snapshot, role binding) from artifacts.

Open questions / decisions to surface:
- Default retention for Dedicated customers under enterprise contracts (legal input required).
- How should PII redaction rules be templated for non-US customers? (GDPR / DSR implications).
- Emergency elevation workflow for Private installs: allow customer opt-in for Redwood SRE temporary support access?

Next actions / owner assignments:
- [Priya] Draft example export generator for SIEM with redaction toggles (target: 2026-03-01).
- [Ellen] Wire up role-change evidence CI step to infra repo (target: 2026-02-28).
- [Mateo] Prototype on-prem evidence agent with signed bundle upload (target: 2026-03-15).

Appendix: sample audit event (concise JSON for engineers)
{
  "event_id": "111e2222-3333-4444-aaaa-bbbbbccccccc",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-14T18:22:07Z",
  "actor_id": "u_1837",
  "actor_email": "redacted:user@example.com",
  "actor_role": "model-ops",
  "action": "models:upload",
  "resource_arn": "arn:redwood:model:acme:search-model",
  "outcome": "success",
  "env": "dedicated"
}

Notes: keep this doc intentionally pragmatic and prescriptive. For official templates and the canonical role matrix, link to the shared spreadsheet in linked_artifacts. Use this guide as the working draft for RBAC v2 rollout and evidence automation design.
